messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue has an inverse.

The recurrence is
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397}.
\]
Because \(a_0=1\), no \(a_n\) can be \(0\) or \(-1\): if \(a_n=-1\), the congruence would give \(0\equiv -1\), impossible; if \(a_{n+1}=0\), then \(a_n=0\), also impossible. So all \(a_n\) are invertible modulo \(397\).

Divide the recurrence by \(a_na_{n+1}\):
\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}\equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}} \pmod{397}.
\]
But
\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac1{a_{n+1}} \equiv a_n+2+\frac1{a_n},
\]
so
\[
a_n \equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Now sum this for \(n=0,1,\dots,2025\):
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2025} a_n
\equiv \sum_{n=0}^{2025}\left(\frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}-2\right)
\equiv \frac1{a_{2026}}-\frac1{a_0}-2\cdot 2026.
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv a_{2026}+\frac1{a_{2026}}-\frac1{a_0}-4052.
\]
Since \(a_0=1\) and \(a_{2026}=9\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 9+9^{-1}-1-4052 \pmod{397}.
\]
Now \(4052\equiv 82\pmod{397}\), and \(9^{-1}\equiv 353\pmod{397}\) because \(9\cdot 353=3177\equiv 1\pmod{397}\). Hence
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 9+353-1-82
\equiv 279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
